newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin raps PM for not promoting young in govt.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin raps PM for not promoting young in govt.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin admonished Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Thursday for not promoting young people into the government and said the young were the best guarantee of future reforms.

"We are simply afraid of promoting the young. Yes we are, Viktor Stepenovich (Chernomyrdin)! Don't worry, they are not trying to get into your shoes," said Yeltsin in a regular radio address to the nation.
The 66-year-old president recently drafted younger reformers, 41-year-old Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, 37, into the government to help kickstart stalled economic reforms.

In his address Yeltsin also appealed to regional governors and city mayors to bring more young people into positions of responsibility and urged the young themselves to become more involved in politics instead of just watching it on television.
"The fighting qualities of the young, their ardour, their boldness are the reserve for the continuation of reforms which we have so far failed to mobilise," said Yeltsin.
Yeltsin's appeal echoed comments this week by Nemtsov, a first deputy prime minister, who said young leaders were needed in both government and industry.
Nemtsov, a former provincial governor, is a popular figure widely regarded as a potential presidential candidate.
Yeltsin ordered Chernomyrdin to rehuffle his government last month after sharply criticising its failure to revive Russia's moribund economy and to tackle problems like wage and pension arrears.

Chernomyrdin, 59, is another potential presidential candidate but the stolid former gas industry chief is seen as lacking the charisma to be able to succeed Yeltsin, despite the backing of influential financial groups.

Chernomyrdin, re-elected last Saturday as leader of his Our Home is Russia party, said it should field its own candidate in the next presidential election, due in 2000, but stopped short of proposing himself.
